entities.name: USER
entities.rationale: Stick-figure actor drawn at far left labeled USER; internal developer who opens the Orion portal (https://orion) to request an environment.

entities.name: ROUTE 53
entities.rationale: Icon at (771,372) labeled ROUTE 53; performs DNS resolution for the Orion portal URL. The handwritten https://orion label points down into it.

entities.name: ALB
entities.rationale: Icon at (941,373) labeled ALB; Application Load Balancer receiving the resolved request and forwarding it to the Kubernetes pods on EKS.

entities.name: EKS
entities.rationale: Icon at (1103,378) labeled EKS; container orchestrator running all workloads. Drawn inside a dashed container together with the SPOT icon below it; the application pod and Kubernetes jobs (M.S.1, M.S.2, M.S.3) run on it.

entities.name: SPOT
entities.rationale: Icon at (1110,526) labeled SPOT; EC2 Spot Instances that are the underlying nodes of the EKS cluster (100% spot). Drawn directly below EKS within the same dashed container.

entities.name: SNS
entities.rationale: Icon at (1257,377) labeled SNS; receives an event whenever a job is triggered to create a microservice and fans it out to SQS.

entities.name: SQS
entities.rationale: Icon at (1260,522) labeled SQS, directly below SNS; holds job state so replacement jobs can detect and finish unfinished microservice launches.

visual_connections.description: Line from the user up to the handwritten https://orion URL, with an arrow pointing down into Route 53: the user opens the Orion portal and DNS is resolved by Route 53.
Arrow from Route 53 to ALB: DNS resolves to the Application Load Balancer.
Line from ALB toward the EKS/SPOT dashed group: the ALB sends the request to the Kubernetes pods running on EKS.
The line leaving ALB runs down and ends in an arrowhead at the SPOT icon: the request reaches the application pod running on spot instances.

Arrow from SPOT leftward to the drawn pod circle, which fans out to jobs M.S.1, M.S.2 and M.S.3, with a curved line from M.S.1 back up to EKS: the application pod on spot nodes creates Kubernetes jobs per microservice, orchestrated by EKS.
Arrow from the EKS/SPOT group (jobs) to SNS: each job sends an event to SNS when triggered to create a microservice.
Short arrow down from SNS to SQS: SNS fans the message out to SQS.
Long curved line from the microservice jobs (M.S.1 area) sweeping under the diagram and ending in an arrowhead at the bottom of SQS: replacement jobs watch SQS for unfinished work.
